paragraphs.source_en:
2 59 M ohini Chatterjee
I asked if I should pray,
But the Brahmin said,
'Pray for nothing, say
Every night in bed,
"I have been a king,
I have been a slave,
Nor is there anything,
Fool, rascal, knave,
That I have not been,
And yet upon my breast 10
A myriad heads have lain."'
That he might set at rest
A boy's turbulent days
Mohini Chatterjee
Spoke these, or words like these.
 I add in commentary,
'Old lovers yet may have
All that time denied -
Grave is heaped on grave
That they be satisfied - 20
Over the blackened earth
The old troops parade,
Birth is heaped on birth
That such cannonade
May thunder time away,
Birth-hour and death-hour meet,
Or, as great sages say,
Men dance on deathless feet.'
